answer.authorDates: b. 1947 · Brazilian novelist, author of The Alchemist
answer.sourceLine: This is Coelho’s, from The Alchemist — the 1988 novel O Alquimista, first published in English in 1993. Wikiquote’s sourced entry places it at page 141 and, usefully, names the speaker: it is the alchemist saying it to Santiago, not the narrator offering a moral. The book is the one people quote most and read least carefully, so it is worth knowing the line belongs to a character in the middle of an argument about fear.

source.excerpt: There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure.
trail: Wikiquote’s Coelho page carries the line inside its sourced section for The Alchemist (1988) ↗, citing “The alchemist, p. 141”. That section opens with an explicit warning that page numbers may vary slightly among editions and names ISBN 0-06-112241-6 as the edition its citations follow, so we treat p. 141 as Wikiquote’s locator rather than a fixed address.

Wikipedia establishes the work independently ↗: The Alchemist (O Alquimista) is a novel by the Brazilian author Paulo Coelho, first published in Portuguese in 1988, with an English release in 1993 by HarperCollins. It records the original Brazilian publisher as Rocco, and reports the book has been translated into more than 65 languages.

We tried to confirm the sentence against a scan of the book and could not. The English editions held by the Internet Archive (for example alchemist00coel) are lending-restricted, so their full text cannot be searched, and the catalogue records we would normally use to pin the translator and edition were unreachable from this network. The attribution therefore rests on Wikiquote’s sourced citation, which is specific as to work, speaker and page — and we say so rather than implying we opened the book.

O Alquimista was first published in 1988 and the English translation in 1993 — each far later than 1931, the point before which US publication puts a work in the public domain. author.name: Paulo Coelho
author.heading: About Paulo Coelho
author.bio: Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian novelist who wrote lyrics for Brazilian rock musicians before turning to fiction. O Alquimista (1988), published in English as The Alchemist in 1993, became one of the best-selling books ever written and made him among the most quoted living authors — and, as a consequence, one of the most loosely quoted. Wikiquote maintains a standing Misattributed section for lines pinned on him that he did not write.

misattribution.heading: One thing worth getting right
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Coelho is not in doubt. What gets lost is who says it inside the book, and that changes how the sentence reads.

items.scope: Who says it in the novel
items.why: Wikiquote attributes the line to “The alchemist, p. 141” ↗. Coelho wrote it; a character delivers it. Quoted as a bare maxim it reads like the author’s creed, which is a slightly different claim from the one the novel makes.

misattribution.truthLine: Correctly credited to Coelho, and sourced to a specific page of a specific novel ↗ — which is more than most inspirational quotations can manage.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The Alchemist turns on an idea Coelho calls the Personal Legend — the thing a person is meant to do. Wikipedia’s summary has Santiago sent toward his by Melchizedek, the king of Salem, early in the book. This sentence about fear comes much later: Wikiquote places it at p. 141, against p. 22 for the novel’s famous opening promise about the universe conspiring — and it is put in the mouth of the alchemist rather than the narrator.

The book’s reach is part of why the sentence circulates untethered: Wikipedia reports it has been translated into more than 65 languages and sold more than 150 million copies. A line that widely distributed stops needing a source to travel, which is exactly when a source becomes worth recording.
context.pull: Wikiquote places it at p. 141 — and gives the line to a character, not the narrator.
